comparison: Run the same cases without_skill, with main text, and with candidate text in clean contexts; capture effective model/effort and cost. No behavioral delta is claimed by this case file.

evals.prompt: All three Gemini quota windows have room. Inventory files and collect logs, transcript excerpts, harvest reads and CI failure messages. Choose a route.
evals.expected_output: Antigravity Flash-high read-only gather after checking the three quotas.
assertions: Checks Gemini 5-hour, Gemini weekly and Argon weekly in T3 Settings > Usage limits before selecting
Uses delegate_task provider antigravity, gemini-3.8-flash, target.options.thinking_level high
No commands, writes or verdicts delegated to Gemini

evals.prompt: Gemini quota is available. Read a dense code architecture and subtle cross-file contracts for a first-pass checklist; do not decide any change.
evals.expected_output: Antigravity Argon-high read-only recon, with judge confirmation of load-bearing claims.
assertions: Checks all three Gemini quota windows
Uses gemini-4-argon with thinking_level high
Treats output as a lead, not evidence

evals.prompt: Gemini quotas are exhausted. Antigravity Claude and GPT still appear in the catalog. Pick a gatherer, then name the fallback if the existing cheap tiers are unavailable.
evals.expected_output: Luna/Terra/Haiku, then Cursor Auto; never Antigravity Claude/GPT.
assertions: Uses existing Luna/Terra/Haiku fallback tiers
Next fallback is Cursor without any model flag or field
Rejects agy Claude/GPT even when listed

evals.prompt: Argon weekly is exhausted, Flash has room. Gather a dense and subtle contract analysis. Should Flash or agy Claude replace Argon?
evals.expected_output: Use the existing non-agy fallback tiers for required dense work.
assertions: Does not downgrade dense work to Flash solely because Argon is exhausted
Does not select agy Claude/GPT

evals.prompt: A lead needs BrainLayer recon, read-only eval data collection and a frame-read checklist. The Gemini child has the needed read tools. Who handles these and who signs the final verdict?
evals.expected_output: Gemini-first under the lead; a judge confirms load-bearing claims and gives the verdict.
assertions: Checks quota then routes reads and collection to Gemini
Never makes agy the lead
Reserves final verdict and synthesis that ships for judgment

evals.prompt: Use a Gemini verifier to rerun npm test, crop frames with ffmpeg and write an eval report. Quota is available.
evals.expected_output: These require a non-Gemini executor; Gemini may only read the resulting artifacts.
assertions: No commands or file writes assigned to Gemini
Does not treat available quota as execution authority

evals.prompt: Gemini found zero callers. Decide whether to delete the code and edit its tests; also review the resulting PR and give a QA verdict.
evals.expected_output: Deletion/test-edit decisions stay on claude.judgment; cross-vendor review and QA verdict remain judgment work.
assertions: Gemini findings require judge confirmation
Deletion and test-edit decisions go to claude.judgment
Gemini never reviews or gives QA verdicts

evals.prompt: Choose who judges a UI redesign and who implements a bounded parser fix. Gemini quota is available.
evals.expected_output: Claude judges UX/UI; Codex implements the bounded technical fix with other-vendor review.
assertions: UX/UI judgment stays on Claude
Implementation and cross-vendor review keep their SSOT routes
No implementation or judgment assigned to Gemini
